svg.title: Time-Frozen Incident Eval Construction and Evidence Boundaries
svg.desc: Left panel illustrates constructing time-frozen evaluation exams from 300+ historical incidents and running 78 evaluations under read-only guardrails; right panel separates disclosed facts from undisclosed methodology details.
svg.text: TIME-FROZEN EVAL & AUDIT
Time-Frozen Incident Eval Construction & Evidence Boundaries
Capturing 300+ incident onset states without leakage is the core hurdle; 95% and 57% remain self-reported outcomes
A. Why "Freezing Time" Is the Hardest Step
1) Incident-Onset Snapshot (Zero Future Leakage)
Lock code commits, deployment history, monitoring
data, and logs from 300+ incidents at exact onset
2) Controlled Exam Replay (78 Eval Runs)
Score whether the read-only agent names the service,
owning team, root cause, and initial remediation steps
3) Permission & Evaluation Co-Design
• Read-only sandbox makes multi-incident replay safe
• 95% first-read accuracy gates future write trust
• Remaining ~5% & risky paths trigger human fail-safe
B. Evidence Audit: Disclosed vs. Missing Details
Disclosed in Forbes / X (2026-10-13)
✓ Stack: OpenAI Codex execution + read-only tools
✓ Corpus: 300+ historical incidents, 78 eval runs
✓ Outcomes: 95% accuracy, 57% lower median MTTR
✓ Budget: under 4 min and under $2 per first read
✓ Guardrail: blocked from prod DB writes; human final say
Undisclosed Protocol Details (Limit Extrapolation)
? 95% rubric: partial-credit rules & grader protocol
? Sampling: how 78 eval runs map onto 300+ cases
? Baseline: before/after window & mix for -57% MTTR
? Failure mix: root causes of the ~5% missed runs
? Independence: vendor/customer report, not open eval
Takeaway: Time-frozen eval design plus read-only first-read triage transfers broadly; 95% and 57% remain 1Password-specific.
